text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: nightly-perf-dashboard detected sustained tail latency degradation for runtime-pool-us-west2. 95th latency up ~2.3x vs baseline for text-gen workloads. spike started ~2025-11-02T03:12Z. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/nightly/runtime/pool-us-west2?view=95p

elaine: saw this in my inbox, thanks. any recent merges to runtime in the last 24h?

amir: @elaine we merged a kernel selector refactor and a small batching heuristic change yesterday afternoon (PR #4248). landing author was @sanjay.

sanjay: yep that was the selector rewrite to prefer larger-streaming kernels when predicted seq_len < 512. also nudged batch_sampler to prefer larger batches for latency/efficiency tradeoff.

kevin: ran the nightly-load locally with the same config (seeded traces). can repro 95p jump. quick paste:
```
$ ./tools/nightly-run --pool us-west2 --workload text-gen --concurrency 200 --duration 15m
baseline (main@before-4248): p95=120ms, p99=320ms
after-4248 (prod): p95=280ms, p99=810ms
profile snippet: kernel_selector.choose(): call_count=1.2M, fallback_to_small_kernel=18%, avg_decision_ms=0.4ms
KV cache stats: miss_rate=0.37, eviction_rate +22% vs baseline
```

monitoring-bot: correlate: high KV eviction windows align with tail spikes (~03:10-03:40Z).

elaine: interesting. selector rewrite intended to reduce per-token cost by using big-kernel for short sequences. but if KV miss rate spikes it could be causing extra context fetches and thrashing.

amir: can we bisect the change quickly? range: commit a1b2c3..d4e5f6 (PR 4248).

sanjay: I can run a targeted bisect on canary nodes. quick observations from local CPU flame: the new kernel path allocates a different KV layout so cache localities change. suspect interaction with batch sizing: larger batches increase effective KV pressure.

kevin: doing a narrow reproduce: run with batch_sampler forced to old behavior and new selector. results: p95 drops to 140ms. so batching tweak looks like main multiplier.

lisa: deploy-bot shows a blocked rollout for the release that included 4248. rollout state: paused at canary due to perf alert. https://release.redwood/internal/rolls/2025-11-02/6789
deploy-bot: Rollout paused: automated safety check (perf) triggered. No further batches will be promoted.

ryan: propose two-step: 1) quick revert of batching heuristic (hotfix branch) to restore previous batch_sampler behavior; 2) run the CI perf job + 2x nightly-run to validate. if still bad, revert whole PR.

elaine: agree. sanjay can you whip a revert for just the batching change (keep selector refactor for later)? we want minimal blast radius.

sanjay: on it. creating PR #4256 that flips batch_sampler to prior weights. pushing to hotfix/rollback-batching.

kevin: queued CI perf runs: https://ci.redwood/internal/4260 (hotfix branch). first run completed: p95=130ms, p99=330ms. looks promising.

amir: nice. can you also run a KV stress test with long sequences to ensure no hidden regression?

kevin: running kv-stress now (estimate 25m). output so far: eviction_rate back to baseline, miss_rate=0.09, tail latency stable.

elaine: temporary mitigation OK. but we need a follow-up: coordinate with @sanjay to tune selector + batching interplay and add a guard in selector: if kv_miss_rate > 0.25 fallback to conservative kernel. also add metric and alert for batch_sampler weight flips.

sanjay: noted. adding config guard in selector: `if (kv_miss_ratio > 0.25 || seq_len > 1024) use_small_kernel = true` and will add tests.

ryan: I'll approve hotfix PR once CI perf passes second run. then ops will promote rollback to canary and watch metrics for 2 hours before full promotion.

lisa: pinging support/ops to hold customer-facing alerts until we have confirmation.

monitoring-bot: new alert cleared in canary after rollback branch deployed to canary at 2025-11-02T04:02Z. will keep watching.

kevin: kv-stress finished: full run numbers attached: p95=125ms, p99=340ms, eviction_rate -1% vs baseline.

elaine: great work team. action items:
- @sanjay: follow-up PR to rework selector with safety-guard + tests (deadline EOD).
- @kevin: expand nightly perf suite to include KV-stress traces.
- @amir/ryan: keep the rollout paused until we get 24h stable metrics.
- @lisa: update incident tracker and customer comms if needed.

ryan: creating rollback ticket and scheduling post-mortem for tomorrow. closing this thread for now. :thumbsup:
